blocks.text: Welcome to your first lesson. Today you'll learn how to sit and hold your hands at the piano, find your way around the keys, and play your first tune, *Mary Had a Little Lamb*, with numbered fingers.

**How to sit.** Sit toward the front of the seat, not right on the edge, facing the middle of the keys: that leaves you free to lean a little left or right as your hands travel, without twisting. Sit tall and let your arms hang loosely from your shoulders. With your fingers on the keys, your elbows sit a little in front of your body, and your forearm is about level from elbow to knuckles: if it slopes up to the keys the seat is too low, if it slopes down, too high. To check the distance, stretch your arms straight out with loose fists: your knuckles should just reach the back of the keys. Then let your elbows bend and hang. Rest your feet flat on the floor.

**How to hold your hands.** Let your arms hang by your sides and relax your hands completely: they curve on their own. Lift one hand onto the keys (or a table) without changing that shape: the fingers make a letter C, landing on their tips, the thumb resting lightly beside them, the wrist loose and level with your forearm. If your hand feels stiff, imagine holding an apple in each hand, then drop the apples: the wrists go soft and the fingers stay curved.
blocks.title: What Is Proper Piano Posture? Tips for Hand, Arm, and Seat Position (Hoffman Academy, 14 min)
blocks.caption: Made for children; it covers where to sit, how far away and how high, and the shape of the hand.

blocks.text:
# The keyboard
A piano has white keys and black keys. Look at the black keys: they aren't spread evenly. They come in groups of **two** and **three**, with a gap between each group, where two white keys sit side by side with no black key between them. That pattern repeats all the way along, and every key on the piano is found from it, so the groups are your map. To tell them apart, look for a gap and count the black keys up to the next one: two or three.

Keys to the **left** sound **lower**; keys to the **right** sound **higher**.

blocks.alt: Two octaves of piano keys: groups of two black keys outlined in orange and labelled 2, groups of three outlined in blue and labelled 3, a gap between two white keys marked "no black key here", and arrows showing lower to the left and higher to the right
blocks.caption: Groups of two (orange) and three (blue), with a gap between them.
Try the black keys: they fit together so well that almost anything you play on them sounds like a tune.

blocks.text:
# Copy the keys
Now get your fingers on the keys. The app plays a short pattern, lighting each key as it sounds; then you play it back. Each time you get it right, the pattern grows by one. If you miss, it plays the whole pattern again and you have another go, as many times as you like; and if you're ready before it finishes, just start playing. Reach a pattern of six and you've done it; then you can keep going for as long as you like.

blocks.title: Copy the keys
blocks.about: Watch and listen, then play the pattern back. It grows by one each time.

blocks.text:
## Extra challenge: by ear
The same game on the five black keys, but nothing lights up: you only hear the pattern. Listen for whether each note goes up or down, and find it on the keys. If you miss, the whole pattern plays again.

blocks.title: Extra challenge: by ear
blocks.about: Listen to the pattern on the black keys and play it back. Nothing lights up.

blocks.text:
Fingers are numbered the same way in both hands:

- **1**: thumb
- **2**: pointer
- **3**: middle finger
- **4**: ring finger
- **5**: little finger

Try it on a table: rest both hands in a round shape and tap each finger as you say its number out loud, 1 to 5 and back. Then out of order, naming the hand first: right hand 3, left hand 1, right hand 5. Saying the number as the finger moves is what makes it stick.
blocks.title: Piano Finger Numbers for Beginners (Hoffman Academy, 7 min)
blocks.caption: Made for children: finger numbers with games.

blocks.text:
# C position
Now put the numbers on the keys. Find the pair of black keys nearest the middle of the keyboard. Put your **right thumb (1)** on the white key just to the left of that pair, then fingers **2, 3, 4 and 5** on the next white keys to the right, one finger on each key. That's **C position**.

For your **left hand**, find the next pair of black keys to the left. Put your **little finger (5)** on the white key just left of that pair, then fingers **4, 3, 2 and 1** on the next white keys to the right.

# Mary Had a Little Lamb
Your first tune, played by finger numbers. The numbers on the screen say which finger plays next; the keys show the numbers too, so you can see which key is under which finger. First the right hand, then the left hand, which plays the same tune lower down with its own fingers. There's no clock: take each note as it comes.

blocks.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
blocks.about: Play the tune by finger numbers: right hand, then left hand.
